name: LWC Stampede

matches.note: Nate Mathis won by pinfall in 5 minutes, 22 seconds.
Tex Violence won by pinfall in 7 minutes, 38 seconds, retaining the title.

note: Two further matches aired the same broadcast (a singles bout and a tag contenders' match) but are not individually resolved clearly enough in the text to structure. The broadcast closes on an angle in which the promotion's own founder-figure Bishop confronts Tex Violence after the promotion's own on-screen founder Ryan Powell announces upcoming matches.

matches.stipulation: Heaven and Hell match, LWC Rio Grande Championship
matches.note: Johnny Rage won by pinfall in 13 minutes, 22 seconds after his fallen opponent unexpectedly stirred to make the count, becoming the new champion.

name: LWC Sunday Stampede

appearances.note: Calls the broadcast from the announce table with Biff Lincoln.
Calls the broadcast from the announce table with Aaron Wexler.
Introduces the matches and announces the results; he leaves the ring when Tex Violence dives in after the main event.

Opens the broadcast in the ring with Johnny Conquest, calling out Pleasure & Pain; when three figures billed in quotation marks as Nik Nyce, Stan Silvers and Tommy Osakgu come out, the Outlaws beat them down.
Stands over the three fallen figures after a backdrop driver and a ball-gag enhanced Underdog, then charges Bob Thacker when his date ends up on the ring announcer's lap.
Hosts the first Sam's Club interview segment and beats Tex Violence at five-card stud with a full house.
Guest on the first Sam's Club; he loses the card game, so he must team with Crabcake Killa for a month.
Leads Pleasure & Pain to the ring for the mystery challenge, stomps Superstar #2 on the outside during it, and is hit with the Shotgun by Terry Blaze afterward.
Unmasked after the mystery challenge; he and his brothers cut a promo claiming the Twin Pistol belts they say they never lost.
Unmasked after the mystery challenge; he takes the house microphone and names Nik Nyce as the target of the brothers' revenge.
Arrives at ringside during the mystery challenge and hits Nik Nyce with the Shotgun, a gorilla press, on the arena floor; he joins the brothers' promo.
Delivers a backstage address introducing Midori-iro Kikai, accompanies him to the ring, and closes the broadcast telling shadowy figures that Kikai's humiliation went as planned.
Cuts a backstage promo before the main event, promising to hurt Midori-iro Kikai.
Answers Ryan Decker in a backstage address with Keru, promising to baptize him in blood.
Dives into the ring after the main event, hangs Ryan Decker with his barbed-wire bullrope and hits Midori-iro Kikai with a modified DDT until Robert Donovan arrives.
Runs to the ring after Tex Violence hangs Ryan Decker and trades right hands with him.
Appears from nowhere with a chairshot as Retribution comes to the ring.
Comes to the ring as Tex Violence's partner and is cut off by a chairshot from Matt Donovan.

matches.note: Billed as the opening tag match. Bob Thacker's introduction is cut off by Mark Cutter's voice; Cutter introduces B. Astard as the greatest rookie of his career, and the Outlaws enter in blonde wigs and dresses to "Nine to Five". Cutter offers to throw the match if the Outlaws beat the Twin Pistol Champions the next week and meet his team for the titles at Last Tangle in Texarkana; the Outlaws agree and the posting cuts to a commercial. No finish is posted.

Eleven minutes, forty-two seconds as announced. Hollywood takes Powell apart with a Northern Lights suplex, a belly-to-back suplex from the top, a leaping Death Valley Driver through a table and a sitdown piledriver onto a chair, then pins him with a Blockbuster. Powell is helped to the back by medics.

Billed as a mystery challenge. Two masked Superstars in plain black gear, who by Aaron Wexler's sources had just signed with the CEO, out-wrestle Pleasure & Pain with armdrags, a thrust kick and a powerbomb-neckbreaker combination. Stan Silvers goes out to a kataha-jime sleeper when the referee's raised arm drops three times; the winners unmask as Rich and Randy Blaze. Terry Blaze arrives and hits Nik Nyce with the Shotgun, a gorilla press, on the arena floor.

Seventeen minutes, four seconds as announced; no time limit, anything goes. Decker brings a ten-foot stepladder and a toilet seat, Kikai an axhandle with quarters taped to the end. Kikai breaks a chair over Decker's head and drives the axhandle into his back and forehead; Decker crotches him on the top rope, hits a top-rope huracanrana onto the ladder, a swinging DDT and a piledriver on the ladder, and pins him with a flying body press. Kikai had been 11-0.

notes: The Sunday Stampede of 4 October 1998, posted on 13 October. It opens on a video package of the promotion's recent history and a confrontation between the Kentucky Fried Outlaws and three figures billed, in quotation marks, as Nik Nyce, Stan Silvers and Tommy Osakgu, then runs the first Sam's Club interview segment, a tag opener the posting never finishes, Hollywood against Marty Powell, a mystery challenge in which two masked Superstars unmask as Rich and Randy Blaze, and a Bunkhouse Street Fight in which Ryan Decker ends Midori-iro Kikai's unbeaten run. Tex Violence and Robert Donovan close the night in the ring, and Keru tells a room of shadowy figures that it went as planned. In their promo the Blaze Brothers say the promotion had stopped operating before they could settle their old scores.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 13 October 1998.

name: LWC Sunday Stampede

appearances.note: Calls the broadcast; Biff Lincoln walks out before the Boris and Kikai match and Wexler works alone with Robert Donovan beside him.
Calls the opening matches and leaves the table when Robert Donovan arrives as guest commentator; he returns afterward.
Introduces the matches and announces the results; he leaves the ring when Tex Violence takes the microphone.

In white suit and tie, takes the ring to explain why he came to B. Lackey's aid and to call out Steve Spector for the two-out-of-three-falls match at Last Tangle in Texarkana on 15 November, telling him he is his toy.
Billed as Mark Wugger, the new Six Gun Champion, he enters wearing three championship belts and mocks the Outlaws over a microphone.
Takes the ring to promise Ryan Decker that their first meeting will leave a mark.
Guest commentator for the Big Bad Boris and Midori-iro Kikai match.
Takes a microphone after the match to accuse Robert Donovan of a plot, then hits him with a chair.
Walks Midori-iro Kikai to the ring and breaks into the exchange between Kikai and Robert Donovan.
Sits in the front row with the WRF crew, then speaks first at the ring, appealing for donations for Aunt Edna and announcing a telethon the next week.
Walks out with the WRF crew for their appeal and tells the ring that the money is for Aunt Edna and not for the WRF.
Sits with the WRF crew, then tells the ring he has loved Edna for fifty years.
Sits in the front row and walks out with the WRF crew for their appeal.
Sits in the front row and walks out with the WRF crew for their appeal.
Hosts the second Sam's Club, is hit with a Coke can on his way out, and is beaten by Robert Donovan, who throws him over a recliner.
Guest on the second Sam's Club; he beats Sam Willis, breaks a framed portrait over his head and chokes him with his own shirt after a remark about his wife.
Rushes out after the Thantasia and Marty Powell match and smashes a banjo over Powell's head.

matches.note: Nine minutes, fifty-six seconds as announced. Veronica Vance walks Viciously Chaotic to the ring. The match spills into the crowd, where Marcus Apollo piledrives Childress onto chairs and Johnny Conquest kisses Veronica Vance and hits Victor Vance with the ringsteps and a chair. The Outlaws finish Childress with a double half crab as he pounds the mat.

Seven minutes, twenty-three seconds as announced; Robert Donovan guest-commentates. Boris leads with a lariat, a front slam and a big splash and drops Kikai with a power bomb that Kikai kicks out of; Kikai wins with the Kesu Sono Hoshi piledriver.

Thirteen minutes, four seconds as announced. Thantasia enters with a Super Soaker. Powell lands a Northern Lights suplex, a Bronco ride and a low blow, but Thantasia answers with a Scud Missile off the apron, a superplex to the outside, a running yakuza kick that drives a chair into Powell's face and an atomic bomb across his knee for the pin. Jeff Bidwell smashes a banjo over Powell's head afterward.

Sixteen minutes, forty seconds as announced; a thirty-minute limit. Tex ambushes Decker at his entrance and the fight runs through the crowd and the announce table. Decker hits a powerslam, a flying kneedrop, a figure-four leglock, an enzuigiri and a flying legdrop, and swings a camera and a barbed-wire toilet seat; both men are cut open. Tex answers by working Decker's left knee, with a dragon screw legwhip, a flying kneedrop across the knee and a half crab with his knee on Decker's head called the Texan Violence, until the referee stops the match. Tex then beats an EMT and throws the stretcher out of the ring.

notes: The Sunday Stampede of 18 October 1998, posted on 19 October, taped at the LWC Studio before about seventy-five fans. Members of the WRF sit in the front row and later appeal for money for Aunt Edna, a relative of Jim Russ. The card holds an Adam Craig interview, the Kentucky Fried Outlaws against Viciously Chaotic, Midori-iro Kikai against Big Bad Boris with Robert Donovan on commentary, the second Sam's Club, Thantasia against Marty Powell, and a main event in which Tex Violence works over Ryan Decker's knee until the referee stops the match.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 19 October 1998.

name: LWC Sunday Stampede

appearances.note: Calls the broadcast; he works the main event alone after Biff Lincoln leaves, then beside Sam Willis.
Calls the opening matches and leaves the table during the main event, bored by Alex Wallace's performance.
Introduces the matches and announces the results.
On crutches after Robert Donovan's attack, he takes the ring to call in a favor from Tex Violence: put Donovan in the hospital.
Answers Sam Willis in the ring and agrees to hospitalize Robert Donovan that night.
Takes the ring alone to tell Tex Violence he is hurting himself and to hold out a hand.
Slingshots out of the ring onto Adam Craig as Craig turns away, slams his face into the ring post and hits a Blockbuster.
Refuses to fight Hollywood, saying he wants only Steve Spector; he is beaten by Hollywood and by Jeff Bidwell's banjo.
Ties Adam Craig in the corner with chains and breaks a banjo over his head, then guests on Sam's Club, where he applies the Kentucky Kloverleaf to Sam Willis.
Dives into the ring to run off Jeff Bidwell and help Adam Craig, returning the favor Craig did him weeks before.
Challenges Tex Violence to a Texas Death Match, falls count anywhere, over his brother's objection.
Tries to talk Rich Blaze out of challenging Tex Violence.
Hosts the third Sam's Club with Jeff Bidwell, insults Bidwell's wife, and is put in the Kentucky Kloverleaf.
The LWC Rio Grande Champion tells Adam Craig that Craig wants to be him, and promises to do to him what has been done to Spector.
Runs into the ring after the main event, stomps Alex Wallace, and fights Robert Donovan through the announce table, an aisle piledriver and the back hallways.
Fights Tex Violence out of the ring and through the building after the main event, putting him through the announce table.

matches.note: Joined in progress, about three minutes in. Six minutes, forty-four seconds as announced. Doe has attacked Thantasia before the bell; Thantasia hits a shoulderblock from the top, a back body drop over the top rope and a Scud Missile off the apron, and finishes with an atomic bomb across the knee.

Nine minutes, forty-seven seconds as announced; Indus's debut. Powell lands a spinning heel kick, a Michinoku Driver and a tornado DDT, but Indus wins with the Cherokee Nation slam and the Trail of Tears, a fireman's-carry somersault from the top turnbuckle.

Eight minutes, four seconds as announced; the Gamblers' first appearance. Randy and Terry Blaze work over Shawn Montgomery, then absorb a double-team flapjack and a flying body press from Dan Montgomery before Terry hits Shawn with a Shotgun and pins Dan with a Gourdbuster.

The main event; Laura Donovan returns after Alex Wallace piledrove her in the first mixed tag. Jennifer Dial leaves Wallace mid-match and Biff Lincoln leaves the commentary table. Robert Donovan hits a Justifier and a power bomb, Laura a flying body press and a DDT, and Laura pins Wallace. Sam Willis joins Aaron Wexler on commentary for the finish.

notes: The Sunday Stampede of 25 October 1998, posted on 27 October, before about three hundred fans. Thantasia is joined in progress against "Original" John Doe, Indus makes his debut, Sam Willis hires Tex Violence to hospitalize Robert Donovan, and "Bluegrass" Jeff Bidwell turns up as the guest on Sam's Club. A billed Adam Craig and Hollywood match never starts. Rich Blaze challenges Tex Violence to a Texas Death Match, the Blaze Brothers beat the High Stakes Gamblers, Steve Spector answers Craig, and in the main event Robert and Laura Donovan beat Alex Wallace and Jennifer Dial before Tex Violence and Robert Donovan fight through the building.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 27 October 1998.

name: LWC Sunday Stampede

appearances.note: Calls the broadcast, missing a stretch of it to the men's room while Biff Lincoln holds the table.
Calls the broadcast and briefly works the table alone.
Introduces the matches and announces the results, including the double countout.
Hollywood's manager and bodyguard climbs on the apron and pulls Hollywood's legs to reverse Indus's tombstone piledriver, then sets up the table Hollywood drives Indus through.
Walks out alone in street clothes to tell Nik Nyce that he remembers Japan and to warn him not to get involved in the title match.

Leads Pleasure & Pain to the ring for the Twin Pistol match; B. Lackey dives on him, and he back-drops Lackey on the floor, slams his head into the railing with Silvers and lays out the doll Silvers piledrives Lackey onto.
Cuts a backstage promo on his friend's betrayal and Big Bad Boris, saying he wants to lose the Silver City title and retire.

matches.note: Eleven minutes, thirty-nine seconds as announced; the opening contest. The fight runs through the gymnasium and its bleachers with tables, chairs, a road sign and the ring bell. Hollywood's manager Nick Dravin pulls Hollywood's legs on the apron to reverse Indus's tombstone piledriver, sets up a table, and Hollywood piledrives Indus through it; Indus kicks out and wins with a lunging scalping that puts Hollywood through a table.
Ruled a double countout by the ring announcer after both men brawl outside the ring with the guardrail and the ring bell and fight to the back.

Fifteen minutes, six seconds as announced; Pleasure & Pain with Nik Nyce against the champions, billed as Mark Wugger and B. Lackey of Bigger Than Hollywood. A blow-up doll billed as Shawna Adams comes to the ring with them and is popped when Silvers piledrives B. Lackey onto it. The champions win after a Fisherman Buster and a springboard cover, with a clothesline from Lackey on Silvers.

Billed as a dark match and told in summary by the poster: Boris beats Wallace from pillar to post and goes for the Siberian Express, but Wallace lands on his feet and wins with Made In America, a leaping piledriver, retaining the title.

notes: The Sunday Stampede of 1 November 1998, posted on 3 November from the gymnasium of St. Luke's Catholic School in Austin, the last broadcast before Last Tangle in Texarkana. The following weekend's card is cancelled for lack of ticket sales. Indus pins Hollywood, Rob James cuts a promo against Nik Nyce, Adam Craig and Randy Blaze go to a double countout, Bigger Than Hollywood retain the Twin Pistol belts over Pleasure & Pain with a blow-up doll billed as Shawna Adams as a casualty, and a Silver City dark match is told in summary.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 3 November 1998.

name: Last Tangle In Texarkana

appearances.note: Calls the card with Biff Lincoln, joined by Bob Thacker for the battle royal.
Calls the card, cheering Hollywood, Nik Nyce and Mark Cutter and heckling Aaron Wexler throughout.
Introduces the matches and announces the results.
Takes a seat at the announce table for the battle royal, his first turn at commentary.
In the locker room with Terry Blaze, worries aloud about Rich Blaze's whiskey and Tex Violence obsession and says he hates battle royals.
In the locker room with Randy Blaze, calls the Texas Tornado Triangle a fight to win without cheating and promises to blow the other teams away.
Opens the card with a promo: Jeff Bidwell and the council could not agree terms, so he has hired extreme little people to wrestle instead.
Interviews Jennifer Dial and Alex Wallace in the ring, then drops to the mat and crawls out when Wallace feints a punch.
Announces Alex Wallace's retirement, declares the Silver City Championship vacant for him and says she is negotiating to manage Mark Wugger and B. Lackey; Wallace sends her out of the ring.
Takes the Silver City belt back from Jennifer Dial, refuses to retire and cuts a promo on Dial, Matt Donovan, Robert Donovan, Midori-iro Kikai and Tex Violence.
Steps over the guardrail to block Dan Montgomery's path so Hollywood can ambush him as the battle royal starts.
Attacks Ryan Decker's left knee at ringside with a pipe during the battle royal, stuffs a silver necklace in his mouth, rolls him into the ring and walks off.
Comes to the ring with Johnny Conquest as Hans and Franz in padded sweatsuits to cut a promo on Pleasure & Pain and the Blaze Brothers.
Comes to the ring with Marcus Apollo as Hans and Franz and boasts about Nik Nyce's sister.
Stands at ringside for the Twin Pistol match, indifferent to B. Astard's promo, and walks away without the crutches he has been using.
After the match takes the microphone, says he alone is Bigger Than Hollywood, puts on a red mask and calls himself El Hijo Del Satanico.
Cuts a promo in the ring against the three men in the main event and promises to leave as champion.
Leads Pleasure & Pain to the ring, hits Terry Blaze in the kidney from outside and breaks a framed Nolan Ryan portrait over Terry Blaze's head.
Fights Nik Nyce outside the ring, is knocked out by a frozen chicken Marcus Apollo throws at Nyce and is helped to the back.
Returns to the council with Kevin Elliott, attacks Rich Blaze and Marcus Apollo in the parking lot after the Texas Tornado Triangle and cuts a promo challenging the tag champions.
Returns with Luke Steele as Blue Chips, hits Marcus Apollo with a floating neckbreaker in the parking lot and cuts a promo calling himself the strongest man in the LWC.
Joins Luke Steele and Kevin Elliott in the ring in a Blue Chips T-shirt.
Cuts a promo on Midori-iro Kikai, Alex Wallace and Tex Violence before the main event.
Cuts a locker-room promo on Adam Craig and comes to the ring in an orange leisure suit to a Gap Band record.
Cuts a promo in the ring before the Rio Grande match, telling Steve Spector that he has beaten him mentally and physically.
Billed as Kotei, accompanies Midori-iro Kikai to the ring, kicks Robert Donovan in the back of the head and is held off by Donovan before Kikai chop-blocks Donovan's knee.
With Sasha Ellison, comes to the ring, mocks the LWC and promises GLCW will carry the alliance with the LWC and the CWLA into the new millennium.
With the other GLCW co-owner, comes to the ring, says GLCW allowed Sam Willis to compete down here and announces the alliance with the LWC and the CWLA.

eliminations.note: Fought as the second Masked Generic Jobber and unmasked afterward.
Fought as the first Masked Generic Jobber and unmasked afterward.
Missed a flying clothesline in the corner when Thantasia ducked and went over the top rope himself.

matches.note: The winner is to receive a Rio Grande Championship match; eliminations are over the top rope and a new man enters every two minutes. Dan Montgomery starts against Hollywood, who is helped by Nick Dravin on the aisle. Thantasia is third in; two Masked Generic Jobbers arrive in a Yugo, turn out to be Jonathan Chaos and Reggie Starr, and are unmasked as the tag team Licensed For Devastation. Pike Rose is the heaviest man in the match, Shade attacks Ryan Decker's knee with a pipe at ringside, and Shawn Montgomery is the last man in. Hollywood, Rose, Indus, Rage and Decker all fall, and Thantasia lasts when Johnny Rage eliminates himself missing a clothesline.

Billed Bigger Than Hollywood (9-0) against Wugline (6-0) as champions, with a one hour limit: the losers get the Bigger Than Hollywood name, the winners get the titles, and if Mark Wugger is pinned he loses the Six Gun Championship. Cutter takes the early running, Astard puts Wugger through a table with a 450 splash, Lackey answers with a fireball and a twisting shooting star press, and B. Astard turns on Mark Cutter with a springboard Ego Trip. Lackey puts Wugger in an ankle lock and Wugger taps out. The ring announcer calls Lackey and Wugger the 'losers', Bigger Than Hollywood, and says that because Lackey forced Wugger to submit he is the new Six Gun Champion; the pair keep the Twin Pistol belts. Neither side is named winner.

eliminations.note: Eliminated at twenty minutes, fifty-nine seconds when Terry Blaze pinned Tommy Osakgu after a frogsplash from the catwalk.

matches.note: Anything goes, no time limit, and a team is out when either man is pinned or submits. The fight runs through the building and into the parking lot. Randy Blaze is knocked out early by a frozen chicken meant for Nik Nyce and carried to the back. Pleasure & Pain go first, Terry Blaze pinning Osakgu, who has just frogsplashed him through a table from the catwalk. Conquest hits his own partner with the Underdog, and Rich Blaze pins Conquest with a Blaze Bomb on the asphalt.

Two out of three falls, no time limit, with the champion in an orange leisure suit. Craig wins the first fall in sixteen minutes, thirty-seven seconds with a fisherman suplex after Spector pulls him up from a flying elbowdrop. Spector wins the second in twenty-six minutes, forty-nine seconds with a Falcon Driver, and the third in forty minutes, fifty-nine seconds with the Cherry Blossom Driver, a vertical suplex into a square driver, after Craig's left arm gives out.

matches.stipulation: Silver City Championship Four Corners Match

eliminations.note: Pinned after a Spinefuser onto a baseball bat studded with razor blades.
Pinned after a Made In America through a table.

matches.note: Champion Alex Wallace defends against Robert Donovan, Midori-iro Kikai and Tex Violence under elimination rules, falls count anywhere and anything goes. Wallace drags Tex to the ring on the bullrope and drives him into the floor with the Made In America before the bell. The match runs through the crowd with a razor-blade bat, broken bottles, tables, a stretcher and the barbed-wire bullrope. Tex finishes Wallace with a flying guillotine legdrop across the steel railing, wins at thirty-nine minutes, fifty seconds and takes the belt.

notes: The pay-per-view Last Tangle In Texarkana of 15 November 1998, posted on 22 November, before about five hundred fans at the Flea Market in Texarkana, Arkansas. It opens on a video package and a locker-room segment with two of the Blaze Brothers. The booked match between Sam Willis and Jeff Bidwell is off because Bidwell and the council could not agree terms, and Willis replaces it with an Extreme Midgets match, a four-way elimination between little-people look-alikes of Tex Violence, Alex Wallace, Midori-iro Kikai and Robert Donovan that the Wallace look-alike wins; none of the four is a registered record. Jennifer Dial declares the Silver City Championship vacant on Alex Wallace's retirement, and Wallace walks out, takes the belt back and cuts a promo on everyone in the main event. Thantasia wins the twelve-man battle royal and a Rio Grande Championship shot. In the Twin Pistol match the champions Mark Wugger and B. Lackey meet Bigger Than Hollywood, Mark Cutter and B. Astard; Astard turns on Cutter, Lackey makes Wugger submit and takes the Six Gun Championship, and the pair keep the Twin Pistol belts and the Bigger Than Hollywood name. The Blaze Brothers win the Texas Tornado Triangle over Pleasure & Pain and the Kentucky Fried Outlaws, and Luke Steele and Kevin Elliott return as Blue Chips. Steve Spector keeps the Rio Grande Championship over Adam Craig in a two out of three falls match. The two co-owners of GLCW come to the ring to announce the alliance with the LWC and the CWLA, and Tex Violence pins Alex Wallace in the four corners main event to take the Silver City Championship.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 22 November 1998.

name: LWC Sunday Stampede

appearances.note: Did not appear for the match; it was awarded to Rob James by forfeit.
Calls the broadcast, picks up a spiked dog collar at the table and ends the night by calling Shawn Montgomery's beating from ringside.
Calls the opening, walks out of the first match's commentary and returns for the rest.
Introduces the matches and announces the results, including the forfeit.
Hosts Sam's Club with Rob James as its guest.
Sits in as guest commentator beside Aaron Wexler for the Thantasia and Johnny Cougar match.
Guest on Sam's Club: says he has the clearance to defend his belts and the Bigger Than Hollywood name against Mark Cutter that night, challenges Cutter and talks about Steve Spector.
Is attacked after the Cougar match by Johnny Rage, who chokes him with a chain and drives him through a table with a Jesus Christ Pose.
Returns to the council, attacks Thantasia after his match with a chain and a Jesus Christ Pose off the top rope through a table.
Is beaten with a nightstick in the ring by Shade and Nate Mathis, handcuffed to the corner and left bloodied, before his billed match with Shade can start.

Poses as a police officer to handcuff Nate Mathis, hits Ace Diamond in the eye with a nightstick, cuffs him to the corner and beats him; earlier he saves Nate Mathis from the council's security staff with a trash can.
Is thrown out of the building, rescued by Shade, announced as Shade's replacement against Ace Diamond, and helps Shade beat Diamond with a nightstick after superkicking the referee.
Announces his retirement at a taped press conference, saying he has entered treatment after years of injuries and drug and alcohol use.
Hollywood's longtime friend and manager introduces him at the taped press conference.
Leads Blue Chips to the ring for the double debut.
Quits the council with an in-ring speech aimed at the CEO of Operations, rips off his LWC shirt and walks out, then returns with Kotei and powerbombs the CEO through a table.
Billed as Kotei, comes back to the ring in a black suit with an ivory cane, taunts the CEO of Operations and unleashes Kikai on him.
Is lured to the ring by Kotei, then lariated, wrapped in barbed wire and powerbombed through a ringside table by Midori-iro Kikai.
Debuts with a promo from the ring, calling the old guard finished and promising to make the CEO of Operations rich.
Appears with his brother in a taped kitchen scene at their family farm in Ash Fork, Arizona, about their losses and a place of their own.
Appears with his brother in a taped kitchen scene at their family farm in Ash Fork, Arizona, doing the dishes in a frilly apron.
Announces in an interview that Stan Silvers has left Pleasure and Pain and that Tommy Osakgu has a new partner, a current LWC title holder, to be revealed next week.
In an interview with Nik Nyce, warns the Blaze Brothers and God's Army and says Stan Silvers is gone.

matches.note: Eight minutes, fifty-four seconds as announced; Cougar's debut, with Sam Willis as guest commentator. Cougar lands a back body drop, a running legdrop, a powerslam and a vertical suplex, but runs into the buckles when Thantasia slides out of the Riff, and Thantasia ends it with an atomic bomb. Johnny Rage attacks Thantasia afterward.

Eight minutes, twelve seconds as announced; the council debut of both teams, God's Army led out by Salvation and Redemption and Blue Chips by Sonya Mathis. God's Army jump Blue Chips before the bell and control the first half. Blue Chips answer with Luke Steele's floating DDT and Kevin Elliott's floating neckbreaker, and cover both men in stereo.

Billed as a special added attraction: the Six Gun Championship, the Twin Pistol Championships and the Bigger Than Hollywood name on the line. Rob James introduces Mark Cutter himself, the referee counts him out after ten seconds and Cutter never comes to the ring. James is announced the winner by forfeit and still Six Gun Champion, keeping the tag belts for himself and Glenn Hudson.

Eleven minutes, fifteen seconds as announced; the main event, the Gamblers' first win in three matches and Licensed For Devastation's first full match. Licensed For Devastation take over with a spinebuster and a superplex, but Shawn Montgomery turns the Breach Of Contract into a hurricanrana and pins Jonathan Chaos. Starr and Chaos then wreck Shawn Montgomery with a gutbuster and a Breach Of Contract through a table.

notes: The Sunday Stampede of 6 December 1998, posted on 10 December, before about two hundred fans in the Recreation Center in Ashdown, Arkansas, three weeks after Last Tangle In Texarkana. It opens on a video package, then Sam's Club has Rob James as its guest and James challenges Mark Cutter to a match for the Six Gun Championship, the Twin Pistol belts and the Bigger Than Hollywood name. Thantasia beats Johnny Cougar, with Sam Willis on commentary, and is attacked afterward by Johnny Rage. Shade and Nate Mathis cuff and beat Ace Diamond before a billed match can start, and a taped press conference announces Hollywood's retirement. Blue Chips beat God's Army in a double debut, Midori-iro Kikai quits the council, and the challenge match ends in a forfeit when Cutter does not appear. Rick Kilgore announces himself with a promo, Kotei brings Kikai back to attack the CEO of Operations through a table, Pleasure and Pain announce that Stan Silvers is out of the team, and in the main event the High Stakes Gamblers beat Licensed For Devastation before the losers wreck Shawn Montgomery. Cards are printed for 20 December in Longview and 3 January in Beaumont.

evidence.note: The broadcast as posted on 10 December 1998.
